questions.stem: 次の表は、ある施設の7月の来場者数である。2020年から2025年にかけて、来場者数は何パーセント変化したか。最も適切なものを選びなさい。

header: Visitors to the science hall in July
table.caption: （架空の資料）

choices.label: ア

choices.label: イ
choices.text: 5%増加

choices.label: エ

explanation_detail.approach: 変化の割合は「差 ÷ 元の値 × 100」。元の値（比べるもとになる古い年の値）を分母にする。

The survey results are worth taking seriously, but we should be careful about what they actually prove. The table shows that students who use screens late also sleep less. It does not show that screens are the cause. Some students may stay up late because they have club activities, part-time jobs, or a lot of homework, and they may simply use their phones while they are already awake. A campaign might help, but I think we should first find out why students go to bed late. In my opinion, a second survey that asks about homework and other activities would give us a clearer picture.

Since September, the Greenwood City Library has stayed open until 9 p.m. on weekdays instead of closing at 6 p.m. We made this change after many working adults and high school students told us that they could not visit during the day.

The evening hours are clearly popular. But when I look at the numbers, I notice that fewer people are coming during the day than last year. The total has increased by only 1,500 visitors, even though we are now open 15 more hours each week. It is possible that some people who used to come in the afternoon now simply come in the evening instead. Keeping the library open longer also means higher costs for staff and electricity. I suggest that we ask visitors when they would most like the library to be open before deciding about next year.
